name: profile-boundary-retention
goal: Retain declared partial workload boundaries from actual child captures through benchmark parsing and verification assembly.

evidence: Native and scheduler child profiles declare partial coverage, but reportedMeasurementSchema omits partial and strips it before benchmarkMeasurements assembles verification data. The record schema already supports the field. This surfaced while reviewing the newly added real child workloads.

The standard child-scope matrix exercises real child RSS, repeated capture paths and failed invocations, but never checks coverage-boundary retention. Extend its actual child capture with a partial note and assert the same note after parsing and verification assembly; keep all original execution and RSS checks.

Sealed red 64ee9dd4 at 360328425 fails the standard actual-child assertion because benchmark parsing drops partial. The prior RSS, unique-path, single-operation and failed-invocation checks remain unchanged.

Add the already supported optional string field to the reported benchmark schema, preserving its type validation through existing assembly. Retain immutable original captures and rerun real native/retention workloads on corrected source; do not rewrite historical records.

Commit ca8a2a433 adds the optional string field already supported by saved measurements. All four standard scope cases, root types, lint and audit pass. No historical captures or records were rewritten.

Same-process frozen red 9d157467 at 360328425 drops the partial boundary; paired green 3f7d3a3d at ca8a2a433 passes the identical actual-child matrix, retaining the note through parsing and verification assembly.

The isolated original-schema snapshot reproduces the missing-boundary failure; the restored fix snapshot passes unchanged tests. Both use actual child-process observations with successful RSS, unique-path and failed-invocation controls intact.
